title: A calculator with a function table
description:
Write a table of five operation functions and two functions that use it:

| op | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| does | a + b | a − b | a × b | the larger | the smaller (signed) |

- `calc(op, a, b)` calls the operation through the table and returns its result; an `op` outside 0 to 4 returns 0.
- `apply_all(array, n, op, k)` replaces each of the `n` qwords `x` with `op(x, k)`, calling the operation through the table for each element, and returns how many it changed (`n`, or 0 for a bad op).

The operations are ordinary functions (`call` them through a register), so keep values you need in callee-saved registers and save them.

starter.solution.asm:
calc:
        lea     rax, [rsi + rdx]
        ret

apply_all:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
op_add: lea     rax, [rdi + rsi]
        ret
op_sub: mov     rax, rdi
        sub     rax, rsi
        ret
op_mul: mov     rax, rdi
        imul    rax, rsi
        ret
op_max: mov     rax, rdi
        cmp     rax, rsi
        cmovl   rax, rsi
        ret
op_min: mov     rax, rdi
        cmp     rax, rsi
        cmovg   rax, rsi
        ret

        section .data
        align   8
ops:    dq      op_add, op_sub, op_mul, op_max, op_min
OPS     equ     ($ - ops) / 8
        section .text

calc:
        xor     eax, eax
        cmp     rdi, OPS
        jae     .bad
        lea     rcx, [rel ops]
        mov     rcx, [rcx + rdi*8]
        mov     rdi, rsi
        mov     rsi, rdx
        jmp     rcx
.bad:   ret

apply_all:
        xor     eax, eax
        cmp     rdx, OPS
        jae     .bad
        push    rbx
        push    r12
        push    r13
        push    r14
        push    r15
        mov     rbx, rdi
        mov     r12, rsi
        lea     rax, [rel ops]
        mov     r13, [rax + rdx*8]
        mov     r14, rcx
        xor     r15d, r15d
.loop:  cmp     r15, r12
        jge     .done
        mov     rdi, [rbx + r15*8]
        mov     rsi, r14
        call    r13
        mov     [rbx + r15*8], rax
        inc     r15
        jmp     .loop
.done:  mov     rax, r12
        pop     r15
        pop     r14
        pop     r13
        pop     r12
        pop     rbx
.bad:   ret

hints: Bounds-check `op` with an unsigned comparison, load the function's address from `[table + op*8]`, then `call` (or `jmp`, for a tail call) through the register (lesson 8.03).
Five pushes plus the return address keep the stack 16-byte aligned for the calls inside `apply_all`.
rules: Call the operation through a register or the table.
